sources.basis: Heritage inventory sets out the ten bays, three storeys and attic, limestone with brick, middle-storey segmental windows, square openings at the first and third levels, and the balcony supported by two columns.
The city measures the top of the attached belfry 35 m above Place Godefroy de Bouillon.
The tower retains paired pointed openings and four corner turrets. Its upper octagonal stage replaced the spire after the 1712 fire. The city hall was added on the southeast.
French national register identifies the attached protected belfry under the same place name.
